reason: Plant fiber and water seem like a practical starting point for making paper for the press.
expectation: I expect a wet pulp or another paper-making material, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Charcoal and water might make ink, but I chose to start with paper.

effect: The fiber and water made paper pulp, so I can continue making paper.
reason: Cloth could help drain and form the pulp into paper.
expectation: I expect paper or a further paper-making intermediate.

alternatives.reason: Making ink is also useful, but I want to finish the paper first.

effect: The pulp and cloth produced paper, completing that material.
reason: Charcoal and water seem useful for making the ink mentioned in the chapter introduction.
expectation: I expect ink or an ink-making mixture.

alternatives.reason: Carving planks might make part of the press, but I want to prepare ink first.

effect: Charcoal and water made ink, giving me another material for printing.
reason: Carving the planks may produce a printing block or part of the press.
expectation: I expect a carved wooden printing component, though its exact role is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Paper and planks might also make a useful printing component, but carving seems more directly related to producing a printing surface.

effect: Carving the planks produced a printing block, which can now be inked.
reason: Adding ink to the block seems like the next step toward printing.
expectation: I expect an inked printing block, ready to transfer an impression to paper.

alternatives.reason: Paper and planks may help build the press, but I want to prepare the block first.

effect: The printing block is inked and ready for a later printing step.
reason: Paper and planks are the only offered combination and may help make a surface for printing.
expectation: I expect a paper-bearing board or another press component, though its purpose is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Placing planks at the dock is possible, but its connection to the press is unclear.

effect: Paper and planks made a lantern frame rather than an obvious press component, so I'll try a dock preparation.
reaction: The lantern frame was surprising and its relevance is unclear.
reason: Planks may form the wooden structure of the press; placing them at the dock is one of two remaining actions.
expectation: I expect the planks to be placed at the dock and perhaps enable a press-building combination, though the dock's role is unclear.

alternatives.reason: Iron may also be needed for the press, but I chose to place the planks first.

effect: Placing the planks at the dock enabled a combination with iron.
reaction: The dock's role is still unclear, but the next step is apparent.
reason: Combining iron with the placed planks may build the press structure.
expectation: I expect a printing press or a structural component, though I'm unsure why it must be built at the dock.

effect: The iron and planks made the press, revealing the goal of printing a page.
reaction: The screw-and-plate explanation clarified how the press works, although the dock setting remains unclear.
reason: Placing the inked block at the press should prepare it to print.
expectation: I expect the block to be placed at the press, enabling a combination with paper.

alternatives.reason: Placing paper first might also work, but I chose to set up the inked surface first.

effect: The inked block is at the press, enabling the paper combination.
reason: Combining the paper with the inked block should print the page.
expectation: I expect a printed page from pressing the paper against the inked block.

effect: The press produced printed pages and completed the final goal.
reaction: The repeated marks made the purpose of the press feel concrete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the press was most worthwhile: the screw-and-plate explanation made its operation clear, and printing the pages paid off the preparations.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the paper lantern frame felt like a detour, since its connection to printing was unclear.

surprise.text: Paper and planks produced a lantern frame rather than a press component.

arbitrary.text: Building the press at the dock felt arbitrary; its role in the construction remained unclear.

continue.text: I might continue for another chapter if it offers similarly concrete explanations, though the unclear dock requirement and lantern detour temper my interest.
